brief: SocGen's morning briefing (10 Nov) centers on the last US CPI print before the December FOMC. Fed voter Waller says he would even consider a 50bp hike if October core CPI prints at 0.3% or higher; SG's own forecast is a third successive 0.3% m/m core reading (above 0.2% consensus), driven by used cars (+0.7%) and apparel (+0.3%), though relief in those categories may not be enough to shift the Fed's course. A firm print should push yields higher with steepening concentrated in the long end; a soft print lets bulls test the 4.81% 100dma on US 10s. ECB's Lane is separately leaning toward a December hike absent a data shift, and BoE's Lombardelli will not rule out voting to hike. Brent's slide below $90 (-23.5% from its October top) is lifting India and South Africa's currencies via terms-of-trade and portfolio-flow channels, while China is moving to slow CNY appreciation through a PBoC FX RRR hike and banks raising USD deposit rates, which SG reads as an attempt to floor USD/CNY.
